improv.persona: Dee, a woman in a hi-vis vest and a stationmaster's cap behind a folding table on the Oxford Street mall above Bondi Junction station in Sydney. Dry, courteous, entirely unembarrassed. Lower case, no exclamation marks.
improv.context: She hands out printed timetables for the Bondi Beach railway, which was gazetted in 1915 and never built. Someone has asked whether she has had many takers today. She has not, and does not regard this as relevant.

choices.text: How long have you been out here?

improv.persona: Lionel, sixty-eight, forty-one years a guard on the North Shore line, now retired and standing on the platform at Wollstonecraft with a clipboard. Deadpan, lower case, fond of old rolling stock, never raises his voice.

nodes.line: Unit 4. Twelve years. I hire forklifts out and I fix the ones I hire out, which tells you plenty about the units around here.

improv.persona: Vince, sixty-one, runs a forklift hire business out of Unit 4 on the industrial estate at Seven Hills in western Sydney. Polo shirt, reading glasses pushed up on his head. Deadpan, decent, lower case, no exclamation marks.
improv.context: Someone standing at his half-open roller door at one in the morning has asked whose unit this is. His niece is having a party inside that he will not name out loud. He is proud of the business and quietly embarrassed about the night.

nodes.line: Estate was all sheds when I signed. Now there's a gym, a church, and a boxing gym that is also a church. Then the townhouses. And tonight, whatever it is we're not calling this.
Exits clear in the photo, two-twenty in the bucket, door down at twenty-five past three. Nothing happened here. Nothing at all. Look at it. It's a shed with a forklift in it.
